steps.title: Source Control
steps.say: The editor has git built in. This icon opens **Source Control**. The number on it is how many files you've changed.

steps.title: Your changes
steps.say:
Every file you've changed since the last commit is listed here. **U** means untracked (git has never seen it), **M** means modified. Click a file to see exactly what changed.

In the git lesson, each numbered folder is its own repository, so you'll see one list per repository.

steps.title: Commit message
steps.say: A commit is a saved snapshot of your work. Describe **what you changed and why**, like `Add my name to the roster`.

steps.title: Commit
steps.say: **Commit** saves the snapshot. Hover over a file and press **+** first to choose which files go in (that's *staging*). If you stage nothing, it offers to commit everything.

steps.title: Which branch am I on?
steps.say: The bottom-left corner always shows your **current branch**. Click it to switch to another branch or make a new one. Our feature branches are named like `issue-12-add-turbo-boost`.

steps.title: History
steps.say: The **Graph** draws your commits and branches as lines, so you can see where a branch split off and where it merged back.

steps.title: The terminal
steps.say: Everything here can also be done by typing git commands. Press **Ctrl+`** (the key above Tab) to open a terminal.

waitFor.hint: press Ctrl+` to open the terminal.

steps.title: Type git here
steps.say: Try `git status`. It tells you the same thing the Source Control list does. The **git commands** walkthrough in the Tutor goes through the rest.
